title: Use Destello from code
lead: The public API, the embeddable player, the URL contract, the rate limits and the data resources behind every frame.

python.body: Every sequence can be downloaded as a Jupyter notebook generated from its manifest. It lists the exact observation identifiers, collections, DOIs and cutout addresses, and follows the SPHEREx tutorial notebooks of IRSA: download, zodiacal light subtraction, flag mask read from the file header, a coadd per epoch, a blink with one shared stretch per detector, Gaia DR3 positions propagated to each epoch, and the citations. It is a simplified reproduction of the Destello pipeline.
python.how: Open a sequence in the explorer, choose Export, then Open in Python. The same file is available from the API:

api.body: The list below is read from the OpenAPI document that the API serves at {{url}}. Descriptions are in English. Interactive documentation: {{docs}}.
api.error: The API description could not be loaded: the service is not reachable from this page. The OpenAPI document is served at {{url}} when the service is running.
api.none: The API description lists no endpoints.

embed.body: Any view can be placed on another page with an iframe. The route is /embed with the same parameters as the URL contract plus controls (full, minimal or none) and theme (dark or light). Only /embed may be framed by other sites. Optional messages to the parent page: destello:ready and destello:frame.

url.body: Routes: /t/{target} opens a preset (barnard, wise0855, epsindib, rwaur, rdra); / with ra and dec, or name, opens any position. All parameters are optional. Epoch numbers are 1-based.

rows.ra: Position, decimal degrees or URL-encoded sexagesimal (ignored on /t/{target})
rows.name: Resolve by name: preset names and aliases first, then SIMBAD
rows.ref: Reference epoch for the difference mode, 1-based
rows.rgb: Three distinct detectors in the order red, green, blue
rows.track: Track mode: frames recentered on the predicted position of a known mover
rows.play: Autoplay (off by default when reduced motion is requested)
rows.partial: Include short revisits as low coverage epochs

limits.body: Limits apply per client, identified by a salted hash of the IP address. Responses carry RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset. Exceeding a limit returns 429 with Retry-After.

rows.build: Requests that start a new build (POST /sequences)
rows.compute: Astrometry, spectrum and other computed results, including the notebook
rows.errors: POST /client-errors (reports over the limit are dropped)

resources.body: Every external source, service and tool that Destello uses or draws on, with its licence and the acknowledgement it asks for. The table is generated from docs/17 of the repository and the text is copied as written there, in English. Where the register says not verified, the provider page could not be read or did not state it; nothing has been filled in.

credits.body: Destello builds on the work of others.
credits.spherex: The SPHEREx Tutorial Notebooks of Caltech/IPAC IRSA: the access patterns for cutouts, the spectral WCS and the TAP queries that the exported notebook and the pipeline follow.
credits.wiseview: Inspired by WiseView (Backyard Worlds): the idea of blinking time-ordered images to find moving objects. No data or code is taken from it.
credits.neossat: The NEOSSat Data Tutorial of the Canadian Space Agency, as a reference for working with NEOSSat data.
